title: Jáuregui, Maru Campos’s Former Prosecutor, Is Ordered to Stand Trial for Treason Against Mexico
author: SinEmbargo Staff
content:
_This article by[SinEmbargo
Staff](https://www.sinembargo.mx/author/redaccion/) originally appeared in the
[October 25, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4893153/jauregui-exfiscal-de-maru-
campos-es-vinculado-a-proceso-por-traicion-a-la-patria/), an independent
Mexican digital news outlet._

**Mexico City, October 25 (SinEmbargo).—** After **80 years** without a
similar case, the former prosecutor of
[**Chihuahua**](https://www.sinembargo.mx/tag/chihuahua/) under the Government
of **Maru Campos** , **César Jáuregui Moreno** , was ordered to stand trial
this Sunday for the crime of **Treason** , for allegedly having allowed agents
of the **Central Intelligence Agency (CIA)** of the **United States (US)**
into an operation to dismantle a **drug lab** last April.

The **[Attorney General's Office (FGR)](https://www.sinembargo.mx/tag/fgr/)**
reported that it presented more than **150 pieces of evidence** to support the
charge against the former official, who will remain in **pretrial**
**detention** at the **Altiplano** prison, in the **State of Mexico
(Edomex)**.

> “After providing more than 150 pieces of evidence, the FGR obtained an order
> to stand trial against César ‘N’, former Attorney General of the state of
> Chihuahua, for his possible participation in the crime of Treason,” it
> detailed in the
> [statement](https://x.com/FGRMexico/status/2114347443454197842).

In issuing the ruling, Ricardo Alfonso Santos Dorantes, control judge of the
Federal Criminal Justice Center of Almoloya de Juárez, granted two months for
the complementary investigation, during which the Prosecutor's Office and the
defense will have the opportunity to present their evidence.

> [Post by @FGRMexico on
> X](https://twitter.com/FGRMexico/status/2114347443454197842)

After a hearing that began at 3:00 p.m. on Saturday and ended at 12:35 a.m.
this Sunday, October 25, Jáuregui became the first Mexican in nearly eight
decades to be tried for this crime, according to the historical precedents
cited in the case.

## Why Was Former Prosecutor César Jáuregui Arrested?

The FGR accuses Jáuregui of possible participation in the crime of Treason
over the entry of US agents into Mexican territory for an anti-drug
trafficking operation in Chihuahua, without them having the corresponding
authorizations to enter the country.

According to the investigation, the CIA agents did not have authorization from
the Secretariat of Security and Citizen Protection (SSPC) or from the High-
Level Security Group to temporarily enter Mexican territory for information-
sharing purposes. In addition, they also lacked weapons carry permits issued
by the Secretariat of National Defense (Defensa), although there are
indications that they were armed.

The events took place on April 18, when personnel from the state Prosecutor's
Office and Army troops, with the participation of CIA agents, located and shut
down a synthetic drug lab on a property in the Sierra del Pinal, in the
municipality of Morelos, Chihuahua.

![Former Chihuahua prosecutor César Jáuregui](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/10/02-cesar-jauregui.jpg)The former Chihuahua prosecutor
faces two court cases related to the operation. Photo: Facebook César Jáuregui

The presence of the US personnel became public after four people died in a car
accident in the early hours of April 19, shortly after the operation ended.
Among the victims were Pedro Román Oseguera Cervantes, then head of the State
Investigation Agency; his bodyguard, Manuel Genaro Méndez Montes, and the CIA
agents Richard Leiter Johnston III and John Dudley Black.

Following the discovery, the FGR seized 55,000 liters and more than 50 tons of
chemical precursors at the property, in addition to almost two thousand liters
of methamphetamine.

The accusation against Jáuregui is based on Article 123, section I, of the
Federal Penal Code, a provision that punishes anyone who carries out acts that
undermine the independence and sovereignty of Mexico with the purpose of
subjecting the Nation to a foreign group.

## Jáuregui's Lawyer Weighs Challenging the Order to Stand Trial

José Ramón Flores, a member of César Jáuregui's legal team, reported that the
defense will challenge the court ruling, as it considers there was not enough
evidence to order him to stand trial. It is also analyzing the possibility of
resorting to an abbreviated procedure, which would allow an eventual sentence
to be reduced.

During the hearing, the Judge recalled that the crime of Treason is punishable
by sentences of five to 40 years in prison, so, if he opts for an abbreviated
procedure and meets the legal requirements, the sentence could be reduced by
up to one third.

This is the second court case Jáuregui faces over the operation in Chihuahua,
since last Thursday a state court judge ordered him to stand trial for
unlawful exercise of public service.

In addition, the FGR opened a new line of investigation into alleged acts of
corruption related to casinos and the use of front men, after the Governor of
Chihuahua pointed to possible irregularities before Attorney General Ernestina
Godoy Ramos.

The case's precedent stands out: in 1945, three federal deputies, Carlos
Alberto Madrazo Becerra, Sacramento Joffre and Pedro Téllez Vargas, faced a
trial for Treason after losing their immunity over alleged irregularities in
the administration of the Bracero Program, which allowed the hiring of Mexican
workers in the US, but in 1946, after remaining in the Lecumberri
Penitentiary, the three legislators were acquitted.
